title: Tenant-Aware Audit Schema Negotiation and Fallback for External SIEMs
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem statement: Customers route tenant audit streams to a variety of SIEMs and webhook targets that expect slightly different envelope formats (Splunk HEC, Datadog Logs API, generic HTTP sinks). When we change the audit event schema (fields added/renamed) or introduce richer structured output (nested metadata, RBAC v2 change details, SSO principal fingerprints), some downstream integrations break silently or drop fields, causing missed security signals and support churn.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware schema negotiation and graceful fallback system in the audit-forwarder so each destination can declare supported schema versions and optional runtime transforms. The system must provide: per-tenant destination contracts, transparent runtime transforms when safe, an unambiguous fallback that preserves original event fidelity, E2E observability for schema mismatches, and admin RBAC controls so only authorized admins can modify sink contracts.

Constraints and non-goals: We are not rewriting third-party connectors (Splunk/Datadog) but adding a compatibility layer in the forwarder. We will not attempt perfect field mapping for every vendor; for complex mappings customers will be guided to provide a transform function or use a managed connector. This project must remain performant: added negotiation must not add >2 ms median latency per event at 95th percentile under typical traffic (verified under CI perf tests).
acceptance_criteria: Operators can define a schema contract per destination with a version (eg. v1, v2) and an optional 'transform' flag in the Console
When a destination supports the current runtime schema, events are delivered in the vendor-preferred envelope with no data loss
If negotiation fails, the forwarder emits the raw audit JSON envelope and marks the delivery with a deterministic metadata flag 'fallback=raw'
All schema mismatches generate telemetry: per-destination mismatch rate, last mismatch example, and a per-tenant warning in Console
RBAC v2: only users with "audit.sinks.manage" can change contracts; changes are logged to audit stream with before/after diffs
End-to-end tests exercising Splunk HEC and Datadog Logs API with three schema changes (add field, rename field, nested object introduced) pass in CI with asserted telemetry
A migration runbook (Confluence) and customer-facing compatibility guide are published before GA
updates: 2026-02-05: Kickoff sync with Security, Platform, and Console. Decided to implement negotiation as a lightweight header-based handshake on initial connect followed by per-event flags; will avoid extra RTT on hot path.

2026-02-11: Prototype: added destination metadata table (in-memory + persisted snapshot) and a 'preferred_schema' attribute. Performance microbench shows +0.8ms median overhead on single-threaded forwarder. PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-forwarder/pull/214

2026-02-18: Design review feedback from Platform: add idempotency key propagation to avoid dupes when fallback store-and-forward is used. Security asked for audit log entries when a transform is applied to an event (approved).

2026-02-24: Spike for fallback store: implemented async upload to customer-specific cold bucket (S3) for events that could not be transformed/delivered, retention window configurable via tenant settings. Verified encryption and KMS key tagging works with Private deployments.

2026-03-03: Integration tests: Splunk HEC adapter fails on nested 'principal' object—added a configurable flattening transform (+unit tests). Datadog adapter accepted nested metadata when sent as 'ddsource' attributes. Dashboard item added: 'schema_mismatch.rate' per-destination.

2026-03-09: Security review requested. Main open item: ensure transform execution is sandboxed and cannot leak PII to transforms supplied by tenants (decided to only allow vendor-provided transforms by default; customer-supplied transforms require sign-off and RBAC scope).

2026-03-12: Code review: PR 214 updated with sandbox changes and RBAC checks. QA to run canary against staging with 3 high-traffic tenants next week. Planning: feature-flag rollout, default off for existing tenants; enable-by-request for enterprise customers.
